Equity

/EK-wuh-tee/ — rhymes with purity · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Equity is fairness and impartiality in the way people are treated or decisions are made.

The new grading policy was praised for its equity — every student faced the same standard.

Worked Example

The scholarship program required the same essay from all applicants and graded them on identical criteria, ensuring that every candidate was measured by the same fair standard.

Equity is more precise than 'fairness' because it emphasizes a systematic, impartial standard applied equally to everyone. This is not just being fair in general—it's the specific practice of measuring all people by a single consistent measure.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

fairness: treating people justly and by equal standards

impartiality: judging without taking sides or playing favorites

justice: giving each person what they rightly deserve

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

discrimination: unjust treatment based on who someone is

bias: an unfair leaning toward one side

Where it sits · how evenly people are treated — discrimination → favoritism → fairness → equity

discrimination vs. equity: Discrimination sits at the far opposite end of the scale from equity: discrimination treats people unjustly because of who they are, while equity guarantees the same impartial treatment for everyone.

favoritism vs. equity: Favoritism is unfair like discrimination but milder — it quietly gives advantages to a favorite — and it is still the opposite of equity, which demands one standard for all.

fairness vs. equity: Fairness comes close to equity, but equity is the stronger, more complete idea: fairness means playing by the rules, while equity makes sure the treatment itself is impartial for every single person.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — equ

Root — equ: even, level, equal (Latin (aequus))

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: state or quality of (Latin (-itas))

Put it together

Put it together: Equ- means 'even or equal' and -ity names a state or quality, so equity is literally 'the state of being even.' Equity keeps the playing field level — every person measured by the same standard.

Use the root in a new word: equal

Use the root in a new word: equal: The referee gave both teams an equal amount of time to prepare — the same 'even, level' root that lives inside equity.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Equity is a formal word often used in policy, education, and law contexts. Use it when you're talking about treating everyone by the same fair standard. For everyday situations, the simpler word 'fairness' is usually better.
